summary: Implemented Issue #2 per-session FIFO serialization: RlmRuntimeImpl queues same-session evals in submission order (no busy), freezes one total deadline at eval() submission (queue wait consumes it), self-settles queued abort/timeout without touching the running kernel, captures the kernel only at dequeue (fatal eviction => fresh kernel observable), makes dispose terminal by rejecting queued entries and awaiting kernel+drain barriers, and keeps cross-session parallelism. Strict TDD: RED on base e55418b (6 FAIL / 2 PASS focused) then GREEN; full gate PASS (focused 8/8, rlm-loop 94/94, pnpm test 103 pass + 2 live-skipped, typecheck, build, py_compile, check:memory, git diff --check).

pointers: RlmRuntimeImpl.eval (submission-time deadline; enqueue only, no kernel creation)
RlmRuntimeImpl.enqueue (queued abort/timeout self-settlement; post-registration signal.aborted re-check)
RlmRuntimeImpl.drainLoop / runEntry (dequeue-time kernel capture; hands signal + remaining deadline to waitReady/evalCell)
RlmRuntimeImpl.dispose (terminal; rejects not-yet-active queued entries; awaits kernels and drain workers)
M2 Issue#2: same-session evals run FIFO by submission order and the later cell sees earlier globals
M2 Issue#2: different sessions run concurrently and keep isolated namespaces
M2 Issue#2: aborting a queued eval rejects immediately and keeps the running same-session kernel alive
M2 Issue#2: dispose rejects every queued eval, awaits kernel teardown, and no queued work starts
M2 Issue#2: after a kernel crash the queued successors run on a fresh kernel only after eviction (namespace loss observable)
M2 Issue#2: a queued eval whose budget expires before dequeue is rejected timeout without starting a kernel
M2 Issue#4: a concurrent eval during a fatal child-settlement window is queued and the next eval uses a fresh kernel (retitled)
M2 Issue#4: a concurrent eval during a live-kernel settlement window is queued until settlement completes (retitled)
Issue #4 active->settling->settled bullet rewritten: concurrent eval is queued, Kernel.busy is unreachable internal defense
Issue #4 终态转换 bullet rewritten: 排队而非 busy/closed

steps: RED: appended six M2 Issue#2 tests (Deferred latch / real Python kernel, no long sleeps) and retitled the two Issue #4 settlement tests to queued semantics; focused run on base e55418b = 8 tests, 6 FAIL / 2 PASS; failures are the pre-queue contract (busy from Kernel.evalCell on FIFO/crash, queued abort/deadline rejected busy instead of cancel/timeout, settlement-window concurrent eval rejected instead of queued); 2 PASS = cross-session parallelism guard and dispose test (all evals queued behind not-yet-ready kernel). During RED hardening only test files changed: fixed an insert-placement error and the FIFO fixture (v.length -> len(v)); neither is a product defect.
RED hygiene: strengthened dispose test to wait until the kernel is provably running before queueing, and attached rejection guards so a failing base cannot leak orphan kernel processes.

GREEN: implemented minimal per-session FIFO in RlmRuntimeImpl (QueuedEval + enqueue/ensureDrain/drainLoop/runEntry/settleEntry/cancelQueued/expireQueued/removeQueued); kept Kernel untouched, kept busy as internal defense, no new public fields, no new source files, no Python kernel change.

Coordinator isolated two follow-ups: (a) lost wakeup when an eval enqueues after the old drain saw an empty queue but before its finally deleted the drains entry - fixed by identity-checked delete then re-ensureDrain if unsettled work remains and runtime not disposed; (b) dispose test hang because onQuery returned a never-settling latch that blocks the Issue #4 child cleanup barrier - fixed in the test to reject on the cell controller abort (deterministic cleanup, contract unchanged). Also added an enqueue-side re-check of signal.aborted after listener registration to close the pre-check/registration race.

Verification: 8 focused tests pass individually (each under 30s); coordinator independent aggregate run node --test --test-name-pattern "M2 Issue#2|settlement window" tests/rlm-loop.test.ts = 8/8 PASS 2.77s; full gate run in this worktree: focused aggregate 8/8 PASS 3485ms wall, full rlm-loop file 94/94 PASS 43688ms, pnpm test 103 pass + 2 live-skipped 0 fail 44380ms, pnpm typecheck PASS 2198ms, pnpm build PASS 2867ms (lib/index.mjs 34.60kB), python -m py_compile PASS exit 0 290ms, pnpm check:memory PASS (47 records) 763ms, git diff --check PASS.

Docs aligned (English authority + zh mirror): new Session serialization (Issue #2) section in architecture.md and its Chinese mirror; Issue #4 settlement bullet rewritten from busy/closed rejection to queue-until-window-closes semantics with Kernel.busy as unreachable internal defense.
Candidate freeze: no push, no PR, no main change; generated artifacts (lib, __pycache__) cleaned after the gate.

limitations: Queue depth is unbounded by design; no backpressure/global scheduler/cross-process queue (explicit non-goal).

Kernel RlmError kind='busy' remains as unreachable internal defense; no public API field was added (namespace loss is observable via typed fatal error plus fresh PID / empty namespace, covered by the crash test).
Full-suite runs executed on Windows only in this worktree; no Linux/CI rerun here.
Live Profile smoke NOT_RUN by design (gated, reserved for final M2 acceptance).

The two Issue #4 settlement tests were retitled and re-asserted to queued semantics because Issue #2 contract replaces busy/closed rejection for concurrent same-session evals; behavior of the settlement barrier itself is unchanged.
